canonical_topic: Volatility estimation via the ratio of two lognormal distributions
definition: Kirk's approximation estimates the volatility needed for its modified Black-Scholes-style formula by relying on the fact that the ratio of two lognormally distributed prices is approximately normally distributed.
core_idea: Because dividing one lognormal distribution by another produces a distribution that is close to normal, this approximate normality can be used to derive a workable volatility estimate for the ratio-based spread option formula.
key_points: The probability distribution formed by dividing one lognormal distribution by another is only approximately, not exactly, normal.
This approximate normality is the specific assumption that gives Kirk's approximation its name.
This assumption is what makes it mathematically tractable to estimate the volatility input required by the modified Black-Scholes-style equation.
relationships: Underlies the volatility term used in Kirk's approximation formula
caveats: Assuming the ratio of two lognormal distributions is exactly normal rather than only approximately so.
